key_insight: Combined computational and neural-network modelling identified an optimal tested HDPE friction stir welding condition of 1500 rpm, 30 mm/min and 60 °C bottom preheating.
engineering_relevance: The approach supports process-window selection for HDPE joints by predicting thermal response, axial forces and defect formation.
method: Develop a 3D Coupled Eulerian–Lagrangian model of temperature, forces, material flow and weld defects.
Train two multilayer perceptron networks on experimental temperature and axial-force histories.
Combine simulations and ANN predictions to map defective and defect-free welding windows.
evidence_signal: Experimental validation showed good agreement with CEL predictions; ANNs achieved R² of 0.91–0.99, while 60 °C preheating reduced peak plunge force from 1600 N to about 1100 N.
watch_item: Predictive performance beyond the tested welding parameters and HDPE conditions remains unestablished.
paper_title: Computational and machine learning modelling approaches for weld quality predictions in friction stir welding of high-density polyethylene
